evidence:
Native KISS archives backed by atomic, GC-rooted Nix profiles. Original code is
MIT licensed. The VM fixture preserves upstream KISS's MIT notices.

`makeNativePackage { name; version; payload; release?; dependencies?; }` emits
a native KISS archive from a producer-prepared tree. It adds no engine callbacks
or runtime requirement. Install it with ordinary `kiss`, without the impurifier
wrapper or global engine hook. Native dependency inventory and configuration
checksums remain available. The producer must prepare a runnable target layout;
this does not relocate binaries. The native VM executes a static payload in a
target root without `/nix`, then upgrades and removes it.

`makeRuntimePackage` accepts `bundledNixStore` and `bundledNixNotices`. Supply a
static ELF client and upstream notices. This omits the default Nix dependency;
Python remains required. Compatible external clients take precedence. Explicit
`IMPURIFIER_NIX_STORE` disables fallback; failed mutations are never retried
through another client. A separate bundled-client VM repeats the lifecycle
suite with an incompatible external candidate. Nix provisioning remains deferred.

validation.value:
`nix flake check -L` boots QEMU and executes pinned upstream kiss-community KISS
6.2.0. It tests native dependency rejection, net failure/offline recovery,
configuration preservation, batch activation, service/account lifecycle and
admin intent, unrelated native driver updates, foreign-root safety, removal and
GC. The guest kernel and outer init are NixOS; Nix is preinstalled. This is not
a complete KISS boot test. It also exercises native recipe construction.
